set.title: Cross-country comparison of chip industrial policy design and outcomes (US, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China, India, Southeast Asia)
set.why_it_matters: Governments have announced very large chip subsidy totals, but they use different tools (grants, tax credits, equity, cheap loans) and have paid out very different shares. Only a like-for-like comparison shows how much public money actually reaches fabs and what it buys. The per-country facts come from other units; this unit compares them.
questions: For each jurisdiction, what instrument mix is used (grants, tax credits, equity, loans, infrastructure) and what are the headline totals?
What share of announced amounts was legally committed and what share disbursed, as of the same date?
Which conditions attach to money (clawbacks, guardrails, profit sharing, equity, local-content, technology-level limits)?
Which projects were funded, cancelled or delayed in each jurisdiction and why?
How do subsidies compare as a share of project capex across jurisdictions?
subquestions: Normalise currencies and periods: nominal local currency and USD at a stated rate and date.
Separate budgeted, committed (signed award), and disbursed amounts.
Separate tax expenditure (foregone revenue) from cash outlays.
List the cancelled or paused projects (e.g. Intel Magdeburg, Wolfspeed Saarland) and the stated reasons.

European Commission State aid register and European Court of Auditors Special Report 12/2025 on the Chips Act (to verify)
METI budget documents (Post-5G fund, Rapidus support)

set.title: US export controls on semiconductors and tools, 2018-2026: EAR rules, ECCNs, FDP rules and timeline
set.why_it_matters: US export rules are the most important set of rules deciding who may sell chips, chipmaking tools, design software and memory to China. They reach non-US companies through 'foreign direct product' rules. The regime has changed almost every year since 2019, so we need one dated, rule-by-rule map. AI-chip licensing and Entity List enforcement have their own units.
questions: What is the complete dated sequence of BIS semiconductor rules from 2018 to 2026 (Huawei 2019 and 2020 FDP, Oct 2022, Oct 2023, Dec 2024, Jan 2025 foundry due-diligence rule, 2025-26 changes), and what did each add or remove?
Which ECCNs (3A090, 3B001, 3B090, 3B993, 3D/3E, 4A090, 5A992 etc.) and thresholds (TPP, performance density, HBM memory bandwidth density) define the controls today?
How do the FDP rules and de minimis rules make non-US tools and chips subject to the EAR, and which countries are exempted?
What do the 'US persons' restrictions prohibit, and how did that affect US staff at Chinese fabs?
What controls apply to EDA/ECAD software for GAAFET design and to technology transfer?
What does the foundry/OSAT due-diligence rule (approved IC designers, authorised OSATs) require of foundries?
subquestions: For each rule: Federal Register citation, dates (published, effective, compliance), items, destinations, end-users, licence review policy.
Which parts of the rules were later amended, corrected or rescinded?
Which participant types carry which compliance obligations (tool makers, foundries, OSATs, distributors, EDA vendors)?
What is the current country-group treatment (D:1, D:4, D:5, Macau) for semiconductor items?

set.title: US tariffs on semiconductors and derivative products (Section 232, Section 301, reciprocal tariffs, offset programmes)
set.why_it_matters: Tariffs change the landed cost of chips and of the electronics that contain them, and the US is using them to push companies to build fabs in the US. Exemptions and offset schemes decide who actually pays.
questions: What is the current Section 232 semiconductor scope (chips, SME, derivative products), rate schedule, and exemption/offset regime, and has a second-phase proclamation been published?
How are 'derivative products' valued for chip content, and who is importer of record for tariff purposes?
What is the Section 301 China semiconductor action (four-year review 2024 increase to 50%, Dec 2025 action at 0% rising June 2027) and how do the two stack?
How do IEEPA/reciprocal tariffs interact with semiconductor exemptions, and what is the legal status after court challenges?
Which company commitments (US investment pledges) earn tariff exemptions, and how is compliance checked?
subquestions: List HTSUS headings and Annex lists covered, with effective dates.
What CBP CSMS messages implement each measure?
What did companies disclose in filings about tariff cost impact?

set.title: Technical standards and de facto mandatory qualifications (SEMI, JEDEC, IEC TC47, AEC-Q, ISO 26262, IPC/JEDEC J-STD)
set.why_it_matters: Standards are not laws, but buyers treat many as mandatory: carmakers require AEC-Q qualification, fabs require SEMI S2 safety compliance on tools, and memory must meet JEDEC specs. They decide who can sell into which market and how long qualification takes.

set.title: US government procurement and trusted-supply rules for chips: NDAA Section 5949, DMEA Trusted Foundry/Supplier, DFARS counterfeit rules, ITAR
set.why_it_matters: Defence and federal buyers must source chips from accredited trusted suppliers and must avoid counterfeit parts, and from December 2027 federal agencies may not buy products containing chips from SMIC, YMTC or CXMT.
